title: action panel
name: Action panel — Tidwell
rule: Instead of burying a large set of related commands in menus, present them on a richly organized panel that stays visible.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Action Panel (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: A large related command set is on a visible, organized panel.
fail_when: That set exists only buried in menus, with no staying-visible panel.
overview: A lasting, organized panel that keeps a large related command set visible.
apply_when: Many related commands would otherwise hide in menus.
not_when: A few actions fit a button group or single toolbar.
agent_hint: Surface the related command set on a visible organized panel, not buried menus.
description: When a product has a large set of related commands, burying them in cascading menus slows discovery and forces people to hunt. An action panel keeps that set on a richly organized surface that stays in view while they work, so related tools stay findable without opening menus. Use it for dense tool suites; skip it when only a handful of actions belong in a compact button group or chrome.
